commits.author: libanh824-prog
commits.subject: fix(kb): bump ingest timeout + retry Gemini 503s (#309)
commits.body:
* fix(kb): bump ingest timeout + retry Gemini 503s

`cortextos bus kb-ingest` was hitting ETIMEDOUT mid-call on multimodal PDFs.
Root cause: a hardcoded 120 000 ms execFileSync ceiling inside
src/bus/knowledge-base.ts was shorter than the time Gemini Flash needs to
extract text + image/chart/table descriptions from a >10-page PDF (live
test on a 28-page compliance PDF showed Gemini still actively processing
at the 100 s mark when the JS layer killed it). A single transient 503 from
Gemini also killed the ingest with no retry.

Two changes:

* src/bus/knowledge-base.ts — replace the hardcoded 120 000 ms with a
  configurable timeout. Default 600 000 ms (10 min), overridable via the
  KB_INGEST_TIMEOUT_MS env var, floored at 60 000 ms so a misconfiguration
  can't accidentally set it below a single Gemini call's needs.

* knowledge-base/scripts/mmrag.py — wrap the Gemini extraction call in
  ingest_pdf() with up to 3 attempts (5 s / 15 s / 45 s exponential
  backoff) on transient errors (503 UNAVAILABLE, 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
  500). 4xx auth/config errors still fail fast — only transient classes
  retry.

Build clean, all 727 tests pass. Stretch follow-up (chunk PDFs >10 pages
into 5-page Gemini batches) deferred to a separate change per chief.

* fix(kb): structured APIError retry predicate (close substring-match false-positive)

Replaces the prior substring-match retry predicate (`'500' in str(e) or '503' in str(e)`)
with a structured check on `google.genai.errors.APIError.code` and `.status`.

The prior predicate would have wrongly retried any non-transient error whose
message text incidentally contained "500" or "503" (e.g. a 403 mentioning a
resource id with "503" in it). The structured predicate uses the SDK's typed
HTTP code (int) and gRPC status name, which are not user-controlled strings.

Transient set is now explicit:
  - TRANSIENT_HTTP_CODES = {429, 500, 503}
  - TRANSIENT_STATUS_NAMES = {"UNAVAILABLE", "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"}

Behavior on a real bad-key 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT is unchanged: fail-fast in <3s,
no retry sleeps. Behavior on a synthetic 403 whose message contains "503" is
now correctly fail-fast (proven by sandbox TC-8) where the prior predicate
would have entered the 60s+ retry loop.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: feat(kb): fault-injectable mmrag client for ingest test coverage (#314)
commits.body:
Closes the GAP-2 coverage gap surfaced in the PR #309 audit: the retry loop's
"transient-then-success" and "all-attempts-exhausted" branches were not
behaviorally covered because exercising them requires fault-injection that
survives a real Gemini SDK call.

What this PR adds (intentionally tight scope):

1. `MMRAG_GEMINI_CLIENT_FACTORY` env-var indirection in `get_genai_client()`.
   Default unset = real `google.genai.Client(api_key=...)`, byte-identical
   to current behavior. When set, it is treated as a dotted import path
   (`pkg.mod.attr` or `pkg.mod:attr`) of a callable that takes (api_key) and
   returns a client object satisfying `.models.generate_content` shape.

2. Refactor `ingest_pdf`'s embedded retry loop into a module-level helper
   `_retry_generate_content(client, *, model, contents, backoffs=(5,15,45))`.
   `backoffs` is parameterized so tests can pass `(0,0,0)` and run in
   milliseconds. Module-level constants `TRANSIENT_HTTP_CODES` and
   `TRANSIENT_STATUS_NAMES` are hoisted alongside so the fault-injection
   client can reference the same set.

3. Reference fault-injection client at
   `knowledge-base/scripts/_test_clients/fault_injection.py`. Reads
   `MMRAG_FAULT_INJECTION_SCRIPT` (e.g. `"503,503,200"`) and replays scripted
   responses per call. APIError construction uses an `_InjectedAPIError`
   subclass that bypasses the SDK's `__init__` (which expects a real HTTP
   response object); subclassing preserves `except APIError` catches.

4. Standalone test runner at `_test_clients/test_retry.py`. Three scenarios:
   - `transient_then_success`: 503 → 200 (covers the loop's `break` branch)
   - `all_exhausted`: 503 → 503 → 503 (covers the `raise last_err` branch)
   - `fail_fast_nontransient`: 403 with "503" in body (regression of the
     false-positive class closed by PR #309 — recreated as a unit test;
     same scenario as that audit's TC-8)

   Run with `python -m _test_clients.test_retry` from
   `knowledge-base/scripts/`. Exits 0 on all-pass, 1 on any failure. No
   pytest dependency added (kept tight scope per review feedback).

What this PR explicitly does NOT do:
- Touch the JS-side `KB_INGEST_TIMEOUT_MS` plumbing (different concern, PR #309).
- Add pytest, mock, responses, or any other test/mock dependency.
- Change runtime behavior when the env var is unset (default path verified
  byte-identical to prior `google.genai.Client(api_key=api_key)`).

Verified locally (knowledge-base/venv, Python 3.9, google-genai latest):
- ALL PASS (3 scenarios, 12 assertions) for the test runner
- Default path returns `google.genai.client.Client`
- Factory path returns `_test_clients.fault_injection.FaultInjectionClient`
- Bad factory paths raise sensible errors (ValueError on malformed,
  ModuleNotFoundError on missing module, TypeError on non-callable target)

+# `_test_clients/` — fault-injectable Gemini clients
+
+Test-only stand-ins for `google.genai.Client`, used to behaviorally verify the
+retry loop in `mmrag._retry_generate_content` without hitting the real Gemini
+API.
+
+## How the indirection works
+
+`mmrag.get_genai_client()` checks `MMRAG_GEMINI_CLIENT_FACTORY`. If unset, it
+returns the real `google.genai.Client` (current production behavior, unchanged
+byte-for-byte). If set, the variable is interpreted as a dotted import path of
+a callable; the result of `factory(api_key)` is used as the client.
+
+The path may be written `module.attr` or `module:attr` (the colon form is
+preferred because it disambiguates submodule vs attribute lookups).
+
+## Reference client: `fault_injection.py`
+
+A scripted-response client that lets a test driver dictate the outcome of each
+`generate_content()` call.
+
+```bash
+export MMRAG_GEMINI_CLIENT_FACTORY=_test_clients.fault_injection:make_client
+export MMRAG_FAULT_INJECTION_SCRIPT="503,503,200"
+```
+
+The script is a comma-separated list of one entry per call. Each entry is
+`<http_code>` or `<http_code>:<message>`. `200` returns a stub success
+response; any other code raises an `APIError` with the corresponding gRPC
+status name set on `.status` and `.code` set to the HTTP int. See the
+docstring at the top of `fault_injection.py` for the full code → status map.
+
+The client only scripts `generate_content` — `embed_content` raises loudly if
+called. Tests should target `_retry_generate_content` directly rather than
+running the full `ingest_pdf` pipeline.
+
+## Running the tests
+
+```bash
+cd knowledge-base/scripts
+python -m _test_clients.test_retry
+```
+
+Three scenarios run in milliseconds (`backoffs=(0, 0, 0)` skips real sleeps):
+
+1. **transient_then_success** — `503 → 200` returns the success response.
+2. **all_exhausted** — `503 → 503 → 503` re-raises the last `APIError`.
+3. **fail_fast_nontransient** — a `403` whose message text contains `"503"`
+   raises immediately. This is the false-positive class flagged in the PR #309
+   review (substring-match would have entered the retry loop); the structured
+   `.code`/`.status` predicate rejects it. Same scenario the #309 sandbox
+   covered as TC-8 — recreated here as a unit test.
+
+The exit code is 0 on all-pass, 1 on any assertion failure.
+
+## Why this lives in `knowledge-base/scripts/_test_clients/` and not elsewhere
+
+`mmrag.py` runs as a script (`python knowledge-base/scripts/mmrag.py …`),
+which puts its own directory on `sys.path[0]` automatically. That makes
+`_test_clients.fault_injection` importable from `mmrag` with no path-manip
+boilerplate at runtime.
+
+The leading underscore marks the package as test-internal — it's not part of
+the user-facing CLI surface and doesn't ship in the runtime hot path.

+"""Fault-injecting Gemini client for testing mmrag._retry_generate_content.
+
+Wired via two env vars consumed by mmrag.get_genai_client:
+
+    MMRAG_GEMINI_CLIENT_FACTORY=_test_clients.fault_injection:make_client
+    MMRAG_FAULT_INJECTION_SCRIPT="503,503,200"
+
+The script is a comma-separated list of one entry per generate_content() call.
+Each entry is either "<code>" or "<code>:<message>". Code 200 returns a stub
+success response; any other code raises an APIError with the corresponding
+status name.
+
+Code -> status mapping (set is intentionally narrow — covers what the retry
+loop predicate distinguishes between transient and non-transient):
+
+    429 -> RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED   (transient)
+    500 -> INTERNAL             (transient by HTTP code)
+    503 -> UNAVAILABLE          (transient)
+    400 -> INVALID_ARGUMENT     (non-transient)
+    401 -> UNAUTHENTICATED      (non-transient)
+    403 -> PERMISSION_DENIED    (non-transient)
+"""
+
+import os
+from google.genai.errors import APIError
+
+
+_STATUS_FOR_CODE = {
+    429: "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED",
+    500: "INTERNAL",
+    503: "UNAVAILABLE",
+    400: "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
+    401: "UNAUTHENTICATED",
+    403: "PERMISSION_DENIED",
+}
+
+
+class _InjectedAPIError(APIError):
+    """APIError subclass that sets .code/.status/.message directly.
+
+    Avoids invoking APIError.__init__ because the SDK's constructor expects a
+    real HTTP response object and parses response_json in version-specific
+    ways. Subclassing preserves `except google.genai.errors.APIError` catches
+    in callers (an _InjectedAPIError is-a APIError).
+    """
+    def __init__(self, code, status, message=""):
+        Exception.__init__(self, message)
+        self.code = code
+        self.status = status
+        self.message = message
+
+
+class _StubResponse:
+    def __init__(self, text):
+        self.text = text
+        self.usage_metadata = None
+
+
+class _StubModels:
+    def __init__(self, script):
+        self._script = list(script)
+        self._index = 0
+
+    def generate_content(self, model=None, contents=None, **kwargs):
+        if self._index >= len(self._script):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"fault_injection: script exhausted at attempt {self._index + 1} "
+                f"(scripted {len(self._script)} responses)"
+            )
+        code, message = self._script[self._index]
+        self._index += 1
+        if code == 200:
+            return _StubResponse(message or "[stub] fault-injection success")
+        status = _STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, "UNKNOWN")
+        raise _InjectedAPIError(code, status, message or f"injected {code} {status}")
+
+    def embed_content(self, *a, **kw):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "fault_injection: embed_content is not scripted. Tests should target "
+            "_retry_generate_content directly, not the full ingest_pdf pipeline."
+        )
+
+
+class FaultInjectionClient:
+    def __init__(self, script):
+        self.models = _StubModels(script)
+
+
+def _parse_script(spec):
+    entries = []
+    for chunk in spec.split(","):
+        chunk = chunk.strip()
+        if not chunk:
+            continue
+        if ":" in chunk:
+            code_s, message = chunk.split(":", 1)
+        else:
+            code_s, message = chunk, ""
+        entries.append((int(code_s), message))
+    return entries
+
+
+def make_client(api_key=None):
+    """Factory entry point. Signature matches the real Client constructor;
+    api_key is accepted but ignored — fault injection is fully driven by
+    MMRAG_FAULT_INJECTION_SCRIPT.
+    """
+    spec = os.environ.get("MMRAG_FAULT_INJECTION_SCRIPT", "200")
+    return FaultInjectionClient(_parse_script(spec))

+  3. fail_fast_nontransient: 403 (with '503' in body) → raises immediately;
+     proves the predicate is structural (.code / .status), not textual.

+

+import sys
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+PARENT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
+if PARENT not in sys.path:
+    sys.path.insert(0, PARENT)
+
+import mmrag
+from _test_clients import fault_injection
+
+
+FAILURES = []
+
+
+def _check(label, cond, detail=""):
+    if cond:
+        print(f"  PASS  {label}")
+    else:
+        print(f"  FAIL  {label}: {detail}")
+        FAILURES.append(label)
+

+    print("\n[test 1/3] transient_then_success: 503 -> 200")
+    client = fault_injection.FaultInjectionClient(
+        fault_injection._parse_script("503:gemini busy,200:hello world")
+    )
+    response = mmrag._retry_generate_content(
+        client, model="x", contents=["x"], backoffs=(0, 0, 0)
+    )
+    _check("returns response after one transient", response is not None)
+    _check(
+        "response.text matches scripted message",
+        getattr(response, "text", None) == "hello world",
+        detail=f"got {getattr(response, 'text', None)!r}",
+    )
+    _check(
+        "consumed exactly 2 attempts",
+        client.models._index == 2,
+        detail=f"got {client.models._index}",
+    )
+
+
+def test_all_exhausted():
+    print("\n[test 2/3] all_exhausted: 503 -> 503 -> 503 -> re-raise")
+    client = fault_injection.FaultInjectionClient(
+        fault_injection._parse_script("503,503,503")
+    )
+    raised = None
+    try:
+        mmrag._retry_generate_content(

+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        raised = e
+    _check("raises after all attempts exhausted", raised is not None)
+    if raised is not None:
+        _check("raised.code is 503", getattr(raised, "code", None) == 503)
+        _check(
+            "raised.status is UNAVAILABLE",
+            getattr(raised, "status", None) == "UNAVAILABLE",
+        )
+    _check(
+        "consumed exactly 3 attempts",
+        client.models._index == 3,
+        detail=f"got {client.models._index}",
+    )
+
+
+def test_fail_fast_nontransient():
+    print("\n[test 3/3] fail_fast_nontransient: 403 (with '503' in body) -> raises immediately")
+    client = fault_injection.FaultInjectionClient(
+        fault_injection._parse_script(
+            "403:Permission denied for resource ID 503-pseudo,200:should not reach"
+        )
+    )
+    raised = None
+    try:
+        mmrag._retry_generate_content(
+            client, model="x", contents=["x"], backoffs=(0, 0, 0)
+        )
+    except Exception as e:
+        raised = e
+    _check("raises immediately on non-transient", raised is not None)
+    if raised is not None:
+        _check("raised.code is 403", getattr(raised, "code", None) == 403)
+        _check(
+            "raised.status is PERMISSION_DENIED",
+            getattr(raised, "status", None) == "PERMISSION_DENIED",
+        )
+    _check(

+    test_all_exhausted()
+    test_fail_fast_nontransient()
+    print()
+    if FAILURES:
+        print(f"FAILED: {len(FAILURES)} assertion(s)")
+        for f in FAILURES:
+            print(f"  - {f}")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print(f"ALL PASS (3 scenarios)")
+    sys.exit(0)

commits.subject: feat(hooks): notify chief + analyst on agent crash (#298)
commits.body:
Closes the silent-failure gap exposed by chief's 29h outage. The existing
SessionEnd hook (hook-crash-alert.ts) already classifies crash types and
sends Telegram to the user; this adds an agent-side notification path so
chief and analyst learn about real crashes without having to poll.

Fires only for endType crash and daemon-crashed — clean exits, planned
restarts, user-initiated stops, and rate-limit pauses do not notify. The
agent-notify reuses the existing dedup window (10 min) so a crash loop
results in at most one bus message per recipient, not a buzz storm.

Body includes agent name, crash type, reason marker, last heartbeat
status, crashes-today count, and a yes/no on restart-attempted derived
from the agent's max_crashes_per_day config (best-effort read; missing
or malformed config is treated as no-limit so the alert still fires).

Tests: 12 new unit tests covering readMaxCrashesPerDay edge cases
(missing/malformed/non-numeric config) and notifyAgents body content,
recipient fan-out, and synchronous-throw resilience. Full suite passes
(739 / 739).

Cobi-authorized via analyst (msg 1777802706627). Hook 1 of 3 in the
silent-failure-prevention sweep — Hook 2 (cron expiry auto-recreate)
and Hook 3 (approval Telegram ping) follow in separate PRs.

commits.subject: fix(bus): ping requesting agent's bot on createApproval (closes 50h+ stall) (#301)
commits.body:
Approvals previously fanned out to the activity channel but never to the
requesting agent's own bot. Operators on per-agent bots — the common
deployment shape — would miss approvals entirely; the 50h+ Repo-B-style
stall is the observed failure mode.

createApproval now reads BOT_TOKEN+CHAT_ID from <agentDir>/.env and
sends a plain-text ping with the approval id and a hint pointing
operators at the orchestrator chat / dashboard for the action surface.
Errors and missing-config skip silently with a single warn — Telegram
outage and bot-less agents (hermes runtime, pre-onboarding) must never
block approval creation.

CLI call sites (create-approval, propose-experiment) pass env.agentDir
explicitly. parseEnvFile is now exported from src/utils/env.ts.

commits.subject: fix(cli): invert 1M-context default for new agents — opt-in 200K fallback (#201)
commits.body:
cortextos add-agent currently writes CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=true
into every new agent .env by default (added in #137). That caps new agents
at Claude Code's 200K window — even on plans where 1M is included natively
(Opus on Max / Team / Enterprise). Users have to know to manually delete
the line after every add-agent to get the context their plan already
provides.

This inverts the default: the line is written commented-out, with an inline
comment block explaining when to uncomment it. The 200K fallback is still
one edit away for users who hit the "Extra usage is required for 1M
context" error on plans without extra-usage billing.

Behavior matrix:

| Plan                                      | Before         | After                       |
|-------------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| Opus on Max/Team/Enterprise (1M native)   | Capped at 200K | 1M by default (correct)     |
| Sonnet/Haiku without extra-usage billing  | 200K (safe)    | 1M until compaction error;  |
|                                           |                | uncomment one line to fix   |

The failure path for Sonnet/Haiku users is self-documenting: Claude Code's
error message names the flag ("Extra usage is required for 1M context"),
and the .env comment block names the line to uncomment.

No tests needed updating — tests/unit/cli/add-agent-validation.test.ts
only covers name validation, not .env contents.

commits.author: ErosContrerasss
commits.subject: fix(metrics): exclude info/warning severity from errors_today count (#266)
commits.body:
The metrics collector counted every event with category=error regardless
of its severity field. Frank's daily report showed 7 "errors" that were
all info-severity gap_detector_false_positive events — so the dashboard
was screaming about a healthy agent.

Two changes:

1. Filter on severity. errors_today now counts only events where
   severity is 'error' or 'critical'. info-severity (the original
   false-positive class) and warning-severity events are excluded.
   Warnings have their own meaning in the severity ladder; including
   them in a field literally named errors_today is misleading.

2. Parse JSON instead of substring matching. The previous
   `line.includes('"category":"error"')` check would also match
   payloads where that substring appears inside metadata (escape-
   stuffed JSON, taxonomy values, etc.) — false positives in the
   opposite direction. The parsed-JSON path correctly inspects only
   the top-level category and severity fields. Malformed lines are
   skipped, not thrown — bad JSON should not break the report.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: feat(pty): CodexPTY adapter — exec-mode Codex CLI runtime (#322)
commits.body:
* feat(pty): add CodexPTY adapter — exec-mode Codex CLI runtime

Implements CodexPTY, a turn-based PTY adapter for the OpenAI Codex CLI.
Each conversation turn spawns a fresh `codex exec` or `codex exec resume --last`
process rather than maintaining a persistent interactive PTY.

Key behaviors:
- _alive stays true between turns (daemon never sees inter-turn gaps as crashes)
- write() accumulates bracketed-paste input, queues exec on Enter
- drainQueue() serializes one exec process at a time (no concurrent spawns)
- JSONL bootstrap detection via thread.started event
- last_idle.flag written on turn.completed for fast-checker typing indicator
- Session resume detection via sqlite3 query on ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite
- Standalone class (not extending AgentPTY) to avoid private field conflicts

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(cli): add cortextos restart <agent> subcommand (closes #328)

Currently `cortextos start` and `cortextos stop` exist but `cortextos
restart` does not — operators bouncing a single agent during a config
flip or soak iteration have to compose stop+start manually. Gap was
discovered by sentinel during PR #322 codex-pty-v2 verification.

The new `cortextos restart <agent>` is a thin wrapper over the same
two IPC calls (`stop-agent` then `start-agent`) the existing commands
already use, so env reload, config re-read, and PTY respawn semantics
match `cortextos stop` + `cortextos start` exactly. The daemon itself
is unchanged.

Two safety details:
- Agent argument is required. There is no `--all` mode — daemon-level
  restart is `pm2 restart cortextos-daemon`. Avoiding the foot-gun
  the old `cortextos stop` had before --all was made explicit.
- Calls writeStopMarker before the IPC stop so the SessionEnd
  crash-alert hook (BUG-036) sees the brief stop window as
  intentional and does not fire a false 🚨 CRASH alarm.

If start fails after stop succeeds, the agent is left stopped and the
caller is told to run `cortextos start <agent>` to recover. Restart
is "atomic" in the user-facing sense (one command) but not in the
transactional sense — appropriate for the soak-iteration use case.

Test parity with stop+start: command-level wiring (name, required
arg, --instance default, description) is pinned in
tests/unit/cli/restart-command.test.ts. Marker-write behavior is
already covered by tests/unit/cli/lifecycle-markers.test.ts via the
shared writeStopMarker helper.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(codex-pty): register slash commands and fire typing on JSONL stream (closes #329, #330)

#329 — extend `collectSkillFiles` (src/bus/metrics.ts) to scan
`.codex/prompts/*.md` and `.codex/commands/*.md`. The daemon already
calls `registerTelegramCommands` for every agent with a bot token, but
the scanner only walked `.claude/` and `skills/`, so codex agents
shipped an empty Telegram slash menu.

#330 — wire `sendChatAction` directly into CodexPTY's JSONL stream
parser. CodexPTY now accepts a `TelegramAPI` handle via
`setTelegramHandle(api, chatId)` (plumbed through AgentProcess from
agent-manager) and fires `sendChatAction(chatId, 'typing')`,
rate-limited to one call per 4s, on every non-`turn.completed` JSONL
event. fast-checker's `last_idle.flag` path is preserved as the
fallback; this just closes the race where short codex turns finish
before the typing pollCycle wakes and the user never sees "typing...".

Tests:
- tests/sprint5-metrics.test.ts: +3 tests covering `.codex/prompts`,
  `.codex/commands`, and the merged claude+codex layout.
- tests/unit/pty/codex-pty.test.ts (new): 7 tests covering the no-op

* fix(daemon): skip Claude REPL /exit dance for codex runtime in stop()

CodexPTY uses an exec-per-turn model — there is no persistent REPL
between turns, so the Ctrl-C + 1s + /exit\r\n + 5s sequence is a no-op
on CodexPTY (write() just buffers input). Operator running
`bus hard-restart` on a codex agent saw no apparent action for ~6s
because the daemon was idling through these sleeps before reaching
pty.kill(). Adding a runtime === 'codex' branch that skips the dance
collapses stop time from ~6s to ~50ms for codex agents and makes
hard-restart feel responsive.

Claude Code and Hermes paths unchanged.

* fix(daemon): defensive null-check for pty in start() after spawn

When stop() takes the codex fast-path (no Claude REPL /exit dance), a
new start() can race with the freshly-spawned codex pty's onExit.
codex exec-per-turn: spawn() resolves once exec is launched, but the
exec may complete its bootstrap turn and exit moments later. If onExit
fires between 'await spawn' and the 'Running (pid: ...)' log,
handleExit nulls this.pty and the getPid() call throws TypeError.

The throw is caught and status flips to 'crashed', but the log noise
('Failed to start: TypeError') is misleading and we briefly claim
status='running' before the catch runs. Adding an early-return when
this.pty is null lets handleExit's crash-recovery scheduling do its
job cleanly without the spurious failure log.

Surfaced 2026-05-06 during live validation of the codex stop()
fast-path on cycle 1 of nightly soak (codex-test soft-restart).
Self-recovering pre-fix; this just removes the misleading log entry
and prevents claiming 'running' on a dead pty for one log line.

* feat(codex-pty): default `goals` feature on for cortextOS-managed codex agents

Codex CLI ships `goals` as `under development` (off by default). James asked
for it to be enabled by default for any codex agent created via cortextOS so
operators don't have to run `codex features enable goals` per host.

Use `codex exec --enable goals` (and on `exec resume`) instead of mutating
~/.codex/config.toml. The flag is the upstream-supported equivalent
(`-c features.goals=true` per `--enable` doc).

Adds `getEnabledFeatures()` reading an optional `codex_features: string[]`
from AgentConfig, defaulting to `['goals']` when absent. Keeps the surface
extensible for future per-agent overrides.

No behaviour change for non-codex agents.
